rederivation.independence: Own code (docs/quality/audits/gt21-rb02-rb04-verify-derive.py): own .osim parse, Horn quaternion rigid fit (the pass uses SVD), own contact runs, ownership vote, force sums, heading sign, plane, ankle-frame CoP. I did read the worker's source first to learn the stated rules and thresholds (50 N contact, 100 N vote, 1/3-2/3 band, 20 mm, 45 deg), then wrote the maths separately; nothing from the pass was imported. The only repo import is the source table reader (gt21_numeric_source.read_numeric_table), data access only, so a reader fault would be shared. Agreement to 1e-14 mostly shows the two implementations match the same rules, not that the rules are right; the physical sanity check and the AB27 marker diagnosis are the independent evidence on correctness.
rederivation.results: All 8 recordings, both legs: stored time = marker clock exactly; pelvis angle and pelvis forward identical (0.0); thigh, shank, foot, hip, knee, ankle angles max difference 2.6e-14 rad with no finite/NaN mismatch; speeds max 2.7e-12 rad/s; composition hip = thigh - pelvis exactly; vertical, anterior and lateral force max difference 0.0 BW with no mismatch; CoP anterior/vertical/lateral max 5.8e-15 m with no mismatch; moments (id/Weight, knee negated) 0 difference; hold code identical on every frame (e.g. 28,718 of 28,718). Plate ownership: my contact owners reproduce the stored force columns exactly (zero force difference), so every contact went to the same foot. Contacts in the 6 overground samples: 57 total, 56 by marker vote, 1 ambiguous (AB27 levelground), 0 events fallback.
rederivation.weights: Weight read from the RB01 subject_info and checked to be kg; BW = Weight x 9.81. Not independently re-verified against the source subject table (RB01 scope).
rederivation.treadmill_signs: Treadmill anterior equals -(sum vz)/BW and lateral equals +(sum vx)/BW for the right foot (correlation 1.0), and the negative of it for the left foot (-1.0), i.e. the prior ESML sign rule with the left side mirrored to outward, as decided.
rederivation.physical_sanity: On all 8 recordings: median pelvis tilt negative (anterior), knee flexion positive (p99 67-118 deg, stairs highest), vertical force positive (max 1.16-1.91 BW), ankle plantarflexor moment negative (min -1.55 to -3.42 Nm/kg), mean lateral force in stance has the same sign on both legs. This is a plausibility check, not the formal sign test.

bad_fit_rule.recomputed: Residual over 20 mm (pelvis, femur or tibia) or knee axis over 45 deg off the lateral knee marker. Held frames equal the stored hold code on every frame of all 8 recordings, both legs (1,3 or 2 bits identical). Force and moments are kept: my force sums ignore the hold and equal the stored force on every loaded sample (no finite/NaN mismatch), and the stored moments equal id/Weight on every finite pair.
bad_fit_rule.AB27_right_leg: In AB27 levelground_cw_fast_01_05 the right leg is held on 24.7 percent of frames (988 of 3,999; 988 by residual, 5 by axis) and the left on 4.7 percent. Cause found: the R_Thigh_Upper marker leaves the rigid thigh. In held frames its distance to the other three thigh markers differs from the model by 29-53 mm (median), against 1.3 mm in kept frames, while the other three markers stay rigid with each other (1.8-8 mm) in both groups. Femur residual p95 is 41.6 mm; pelvis and tibia are 5.8 and 4.7 mm. Held frames come in 34 short runs. Ledger-wide AB27 right is 22.1 percent, left 3.0 percent. So the hold is a real bad fit (a marker that moved or was mislabeled), not a threshold artifact. The three remaining thigh markers fit consistently, so a refit without R_Thigh_Upper could recover those frames; that is a method change and is left to the owner and José, not done here.

esml_comparison.what_the_csv_counts: Per segment (ESML rows, ipsi leg) counts against the OLD converter's single plate: reassigned (converter plate loaded but not this foot's), recovered (this foot loads another plate), flagged (no measured force for this foot), changed. They are differences from the old converter, which our outputs do not carry, so plate reassignment counts cannot be compared one for one.
esml_comparison.coverage: The CSV covers 15 participants (AB06-11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21, 24, 25, 30). It has no rows for AB12, 15, 17, 19, 23, 28 or AB27. Of my 8 recordings only AB09 ramp, AB10 ramp, AB09 stair, AB21 stair and AB16 treadmill_07_01 have a row.
esml_comparison.closest_comparable: Share of stance rows with no measured force for the foot. ESML flagged / ours (stance samples with no loaded plate): ramp_2_l 66% / 67%; ramp_5_l 50% / 65%; stair_3_r 34% / 60%; stair_4_r 34% / 57%; treadmill_07_01 0% / 0.4%. Treadmill agrees; overground ramp_2_l agrees; ramp_5_l and stairs differ by 15-26 points. Not like for like: ESML rows come from its segmentation (stance rows 755-1,333 versus ours 2,621-4,550 samples per recording on the whole recording, all walking bouts and both feet) so the gap is expected but not proven benign.
esml_comparison.whole_table_context: ESML across its 15 participants: changed rows over stance rows 38 percent levelground, 38 ramp, 49 stair, 3 treadmill. Treadmill assignments barely change versus the old converter, overground ones change a lot, which matches our finding that the marker vote disagrees with a fixed plate guess overground. Our ledger totals: 29,268 marker-vote contacts, 72 events fallback, 68 ambiguous, 80 unassigned, over all recordings.
esml_comparison.conclusion: Listed, not tuned. Direction agrees (treadmill almost no reassignment, overground heavy). A one-to-one per-contact comparison needs either the old converter plate column or the ESML parquet, which the port rule forbids opening. Remaining difference stays an open item for RB05 readback.

extra_findings: Combined plate: in AB30 levelground_cw_slow_01_01 the Combined plate is a separate walkway plate (loaded 860 samples, never overlaps another plate above 50 N, median 676 N, correlation with other plates 0.06-0.09). It is not a sum of the others, so owning it with an FP plate is not a double count. Ledger-wide it is owned by the right foot in 657 contacts and the left in 6 (position of the plate, not checked further).

Caveat for RB03/RB05: in levelground recordings the Treadmill_R and Treadmill_L plates carry a small offset (median about 13 N). Contacts on them can span a whole recording (AB30 levelground_cw_slow_01_01: contact 0-6340 samples), so the owning foot gets about 0.02 BW vertical force during swing and plate_loaded_left is true on 6,340 of 6,340 samples (right 6,325). plate_loaded is therefore not a contact indicator in such recordings; use stance events or a force threshold. Not an error in the method (the value is measured) but segmentation must not use plate_loaded as contact.

Ledger-wide simultaneously owned plates: levelground 17 right-leg and 6 left-leg recordings (3,456 and 3,140 samples), stairs 9 recordings (45 samples), ramp 2 recordings (2 samples). These are feet owning two plates at once (straddling or an offset plate), counted in the ledger, not checked individually.

decision.reasons: Numbers in the tables are correct as far as an independent derivation can tell, but three acceptance items written into the tasks were never run (MATLAB-pilot 1e-9, six-participant sign test, pelvis range check). They are comparisons against references; a failure there would change the tables only if it exposes a systematic error. Suggest RB03 may start on these tables while the three items run, since RB03 reads the same Parquet and nothing found here changes them. That is a scope call for José.

v2.scope: The worker's three post-verifier acceptance items, spot-checked with my own code (docs/quality/audits/gt21-rb02-rb04-verify-v2-force.py and ...-v2-pelvis.py). Probes ran under prlimit 900 MiB address space (the table reader needs more than 600), nice 19, one recording at a time, peak under 300 MiB.

item1_matlab_force_1e-9.my_check: AB06 levelground_ccw_fast_01_01, 3 loaded cycle/leg cases. Linear interpolation of the raw 1 kHz plate vertical force (best single plate: Combined, FP2, FP1) at the cycle's 150 phase times reproduces the MATLAB-fixed file to 2e-16 to 2e-14 BW. The same force routed 1 kHz to the 200 Hz marker clock and then to the phase times differs from MATLAB by 0.037, 0.015 and 0.091 BW (the two routes differ by the same amounts). The worker's reported maxima (0.09 BW vertical in the worst cycles) match.
item1_matlab_force_1e-9.reading: So MATLAB equals interpolation of the 1 kHz plate, and the gap is the extra 200 Hz step at impact transients: a resampling difference, not a port difference. The 1e-9 criterion holds on shared sample times (the worker's 1,040 pairs, max 0.0). RB05 must take phase forces from the plate rate, or state a tolerance of at least 0.2 BW vertical (worst seen 0.21), which is large for impact peaks.
item1_matlab_force_1e-9.not_resolved: Unloaded feet: the pass writes exactly 0 where MATLAB kept raw shear noise (up to 0.11 BW). See the zero-fill finding below.

item2_sign_test.verdict: counts reproduce; scope is the authors' source channels
item2_sign_test.my_check: Recounted the 648 records in gt21-rb04-sign-test-new6-probe.json: 319 applied_correct, 204 suggested_correct, 125 abstain, 0 wrong, 0 conflict; per-channel counts equal the worker's table (knee power 72 of 72 abstained). Power: recomputed as moment x our speed under D-REF-5, so abstentions there do not matter.
item2_sign_test.scope_note: The detector tests the authors' ik/id/jp signs against rule B, which supports the id sign map the pass uses (knee flexor = minus knee_angle moment). It does not test the pass's own columns. For those I ran a plausibility check on 12 recordings (levelground and stair, one each from AB12, 15, 17, 19, 23, 28, seeded): knee flexion positive (p99 68-112 deg), vertical force positive (max 1.08-1.99 BW), ankle plantarflexor moment negative (min -1.27 to -3.52 Nm/kg), pelvis tilt negative. All consistent with the rule. Probe used RLIMIT_AS 1.5 GiB (above the 600 MiB I was given); peak 231 MiB RSS.

item3_pelvis_vs_ik.my_check: 9 seeded recordings (seed 20261209; AB17, AB28, AB19; levelground, ramp, treadmill). Own rotation maths: forward-axis elevation of Rz(tilt) Rx(list) Ry(rotation) from the authors' ik, against the pass pelvis angle, both median-removed. RMS 1.08-2.17 deg (2.17, 1.08, 1.09, 1.42, 1.90, 1.35, 1.51, 1.70, 1.72); correlation +0.70 to +0.95 with the pass's sign (the opposite sign gives -0.70 to -0.95 and 3-8 deg RMS). Inside the 2.7 deg bound and the worker's 0.62-2.17.
item3_pelvis_vs_ik.note: Median removal hides any constant offset. Pass medians are -4 to -9 deg for most participants but about -24 to -27 deg for AB28 in all three modes; consistent within the participant, so it looks like marker placement or posture, not a sign error. Flagged, not tested.

new_finding_zero_fill.what: In stance with no loaded plate the stored vertical force is exactly 0, not missing. Checked on 12 recordings of the six new participants: every stance-without-plate sample is 0 (e.g. AB12 levelground right 1,597 of 1,597, AB23 levelground right 3,112 of 3,112), none NaN. That is 29-67 percent of stance samples overground (earlier probe: 53-67 percent for the AB27, AB09, AB10 ramps and stairs).
new_finding_zero_fill.why_it_matters: Acceptance for RB02 says unassigned legs stay missing, the pass module says missing stays missing, and AGENTS.md says unavailable measurements are never invented and a missing signal is not evidence. A zero looks like a measured unloaded foot. The columns stance_* and plate_loaded_* can recover the distinction, but plate_loaded is unreliable in levelground trials (true on every sample in AB30 levelground_cw_slow_01_01) because the treadmill plates carry about 13 N of offset.
new_finding_zero_fill.cheapest_fix: No rerun needed: RB03/RB05 can set force (and CoP, already missing) to missing wherever event stance is true and no plate above a stated threshold (for example 50 N) is owned by the foot, and use the same rule instead of plate_loaded. Or rerun the pass with NaN. This is the owner's choice and José's if it changes what a release states.
